newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends lower succumbing to weak crude.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends lower succumbing to weak crude.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices fell sharply Friday after weak crude prices in the last two sessions finally forced funds to take profits in gasoline which had so far bucked declines, dealers said.
"We are back on the defensive again," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives in New York, noting spot crude is tucked into a $19.00 to $20.00 range again.
"Gasoline had been holding up while everything else broke down. But, there was so much length concentrated in gasoline that funds finally began liquidating it," said Bentz.
June gasoline ended 2.11 cents lower at $60.52 a gallon.
June crude ended 31 cents a barrel lower at $19.60, falling 84 cents since April 30.
June heating oil ended 1.31 cents a gallon at 53.02 cents.

Prompt heat fell as low as 52.70 cents, slightly breaching a two-year trendline that extends from the March 15, 1995 low of 44.05 through the June 7, 1996 low of 49.20 on the spot continuation chart. June heat closed above the trendline and maintained it, but heating oil is seasonally out of favor.
Dealers said crude's weakness reflects rising supplies in the U.S. Gulf Coast which is where the highest demand is due to the concentration of refineries in the area.
Meanwhile, dealers said gasoline should hold the 60.00 cent level in the near term as it represents good value in the spring and summer months, the seasonally strongest period for demand.
